articles.title: A Chinese Cancer Drug Just Beat the Global Gold Standard for Lung Cancer. It Is the First From Asia to Earn a Plenary at ASCO in 61 Years.
articles.excerpt: Ivonescimab reduced the risk of death by 34 per cent in advanced squamous lung cancer. The results were published in The Lancet the same day. For Indian families watching air-pollution-driven cancer rates climb, the implications are significant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The WHO Just Endorsed a $1 Antibiotic Pill That Prevents Syphilis and Chlamydia After Sex. It Is Their First Recommendation of Its Kind.
articles.excerpt: Doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis can reduce syphilis and chlamydia by up to 80 per cent. With STI rates rising sharply in India and across the diaspora, the decision could reshape sexual health prevention worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Asian Adults in the US Have 30 Per Cent Prediabetes by Age 45. They Also Report the Healthiest Diets. A Major Study Says the Paradox Is Real.
articles.excerpt: The MASALA study followed 2,700 adults for a decade and found that South Asians develop cardiovascular risk factors earlier than every other ethnic group — despite doing many of the right things.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Surgeon General Just Classified Youth Screen Time as a Public Health Crisis. More Than Half of Teens Are on Their Phones Past Midnight.
articles.excerpt: A new JAMA Pediatrics study found that 50 per cent of American teenagers spend up to an hour on their phones between 10 PM and 6 AM on school nights. The federal advisory calls for immediate parental action.

sources.label: US Department of Health and Human Services / Office of the Surgeon General

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Daily Pill Just Doubled Survival in Advanced Pancreatic Cancer. It Is the First Drug to Ever Do This.
articles.excerpt: Daraxonrasib cut the risk of death by 60 per cent in a 500-person trial. The results, presented at ASCO 2026 and published in the NEJM, are being called the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer in decades.

sources.label: The New England Journal of Medicine

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Study of 540,000 People Found That Exercise at Work Does Not Protect Your Health the Way Leisure Exercise Does. The Genetics Are Different.
articles.excerpt: A Nature Genetics study using data from the Million Veteran Program and UK Biobank found that leisure-time physical activity has distinct genetic pathways and uniquely protects against diabetes, heart failure and early death.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The FDA Just Approved Inhaled Insulin for Children. For South Asian Families Managing Diabetes, the Needle Era May Finally Be Ending.
articles.excerpt: Afrezza, the first needle-free mealtime insulin for kids aged six and above, costs $35 a month and mimics the body's natural insulin response more closely than injections do.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Drug That Blocks Cortisol Just Cut the Risk of Death From Ovarian Cancer by 35 Per Cent. No Biomarker Testing Was Required.
articles.excerpt: The Phase 3 ROSELLA trial found that adding the cortisol-blocking drug relacorilant to chemotherapy extended survival in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer patients — regardless of prior treatment history. The results, presented at ASCO 2026, could establish a new standard of care.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Head-to-Head Trial Found That One Prostate Cancer Drug Causes Half the Cognitive Decline of Another. Every Patient Who Switched Was on the Worse Drug.
articles.excerpt: The ARACOG trial, presented at ASCO 2026, is the first rigorous comparison of how two standard prostate cancer drugs affect memory, attention, and executive function. The results may change how doctors and families approach treatment decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Study of 139 Cancer Patients Found That Getting Immunotherapy in the Morning Cut Recurrence by 77 Per Cent. The Only Change Was the Clock.
articles.excerpt: Multiple ASCO 2026 presentations and a randomised trial in Nature Medicine now confirm that circadian timing of cancer treatment is not a footnote — it may be one of the most powerful free interventions in oncology.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated risks for several cancers including breast, oral, and stomach. Nearly five million Indian Americans navigate a healthcare system where treatment timing is assigned by clinic convenience, not biology. This zero-cost intervention — simply requesting a morning infusion slot — could meaningfully improve outcomes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mounjaro Outperformed Every Other GLP-1 Drug in a Two-Year Trial of Early Type 2 Diabetes Patients. 60 Per Cent Achieved Normal Blood Sugar.
articles.excerpt: The SURPASS-EARLY trial found that tirzepatide helped recently diagnosed patients reach glycaemic targets 4 to 12 weeks faster than semaglutide and produced sustained normal HbA1c levels in more than double the patients on competing drugs.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest type 2 diabetes rates globally — 23 per cent prevalence among Indian Americans vs 11 per cent in the general US population. They develop diabetes a decade earlier and at lower BMI thresholds, making early aggressive treatment even more critical. The SURPASS-EARLY data directly supports earlier intervention with tirzepatide for this population.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Studies Just Proved That Long COVID Neurological Symptoms Are Caused by the Body Attacking Itself. Existing Drugs May Already Work.
articles.excerpt: Autoantibodies from long COVID patients caused fatigue, pain, and nerve damage when transferred to healthy mice — even two years after infection. Researchers say millions could benefit from immunotherapy treatments already on the market.

sources.label: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

articles.nri_angle: India experienced one of the world's most severe COVID waves, with seroprevalence above 90 per cent by mid-2022. South Asians in the US, UK, and Canada report higher rates of post-COVID fatigue and cognitive complaints than the general population. The autoantibody finding offers a testable biomarker and a path to targeted treatment for millions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Just 10 Minutes of AI Use Can Measurably Weaken Your Problem-Solving Skills. A New Study Says the Damage May Compound Over Time.
articles.excerpt: Participants who asked ChatGPT for direct answers performed significantly worse when the tool was taken away. Those who used it for hints did not. The distinction matters for every knowledge worker in the diaspora.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans are the most tech-forward ethnic group in the US, with disproportionate representation in engineering, data science, and product management — exactly the roles where AI tools are most deeply embedded. The study's findings directly challenge the efficiency narrative that many diaspora professionals have built their careers around.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 17-Year Study of 82,000 People Found That Ultraprocessed Food Raises Your Risk of Dying by 10 Per Cent. The Damage Starts in Childhood.
articles.excerpt: The highest consumers also faced a 20 per cent higher risk of dying from nervous system diseases and a 28 per cent higher risk from other causes. A separate study found the cardiovascular toll begins in preschool.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Insomnia Triples Breast Cancer Risk in Women Under 50. A Study of 19 Million People Just Presented the Numbers at ASCO.
articles.excerpt: The largest real-world analysis of its kind found that young women diagnosed with insomnia faced up to three times the risk of hormone-related cancers. Bowel cancer risk nearly doubled regardless of gender.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 10-Year Study of 2,871 Workers Found That Sleep and Diet Protect Against Chronic Stress Better Than Exercise Does.
articles.excerpt: The Canadian study tracked five health behaviours over a decade and found that sleep quality was the single strongest buffer against the health toll of sustained work stress. Exercise helped overall health but did not specifically counteract stress.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Simple Urine Test Can Now Screen Children for Autism. It Measures Gut Bacteria Compounds That Are Up to 1,000 Times Higher in Affected Kids.
articles.excerpt: Researchers at Arizona State University have developed a screening tool that analyses 17 microbial metabolites in urine to identify children at risk of autism spectrum disorder. For Indian-American parents navigating long diagnostic waitlists, this could be transformative.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro May Slow Cancer Spread by Up to 50 Per Cent. A Cleveland Clinic Study of Seven Tumour Types Just Changed the Conversation.
articles.excerpt: The first large study to track cancer progression in GLP-1 users found significant reductions in lung, breast, colorectal, and liver cancer spread. South Asians, who face elevated diabetes and cancer risk, have particular reason to pay attention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Drug Just Cured One in Five Chronic Hepatitis B Patients. India Has 40 Million Carriers. This Is the Biggest Breakthrough in Decades.
articles.excerpt: GSK's bepirovirsen achieved a functional cure in 19 per cent of patients after just six months of weekly injections — in a disease where the current cure rate is less than 1 per cent. For South Asians, who carry a disproportionate burden of the virus, the implications are enormous.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Bedroom May Be Too Hot for Your Heart. A Study Found That Sleeping Above 26°C Nearly Triples the Risk of Reduced Cardiac Recovery.
articles.excerpt: An Australian study of overnight bedroom temperatures found a dose-response relationship with heart rate variability. For South Asians — who already carry elevated cardiovascular risk — the implications are especially urgent as summer begins.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Europe Just Recorded Its Deadliest May Heatwave. Seven People Died in France Alone. As US Summer Approaches, Here Is What Heat Actually Does to Your Body.
articles.excerpt: Temperatures 15°C above normal are breaking records across Western Europe. For Indian American families heading into summer — or planning trips to India — the science of heat illness is worth understanding before June arrives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Cases of Flesh-Eating Bacteria Have Already Hit Florida This Year. The Season Is Starting Earlier Than Ever.
articles.excerpt: Vibrio vulnificus thrives in warm coastal waters and can turn a small cut into a medical emergency within hours. Indian Americans along the Gulf Coast and in South Florida should know the warning signs before summer beach season begins.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Review of 19 Clinical Trials Found That Turmeric With Black Pepper Consistently Lowers Inflammation. Your Grandmother's Haldi Doodh Was Doing More Than You Thought.
articles.excerpt: The combination of curcumin and piperine reduced CRP, IL-6, and oxidative stress markers across metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease patients — conditions that disproportionately affect South Asians.
articles.image_caption: Turmeric combined with black pepper — the traditional Indian remedy now backed by clinical evidence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Genetic Variant Carried by 1 in 13 South Asians Makes the Standard Diabetes Blood Test Unreliable. Researchers Say Thousands of Cases Are Being Missed.
articles.excerpt: Two separate studies have found that common genetic variants in South Asian and Black populations artificially lower HbA1c results — the test your doctor uses to diagnose and monitor diabetes. The implications for the Indian diaspora are enormous.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wildfire Smoke Does Not Just Burn Your Lungs. A Growing Body of Research Says It Is Rewiring Your Brain.
articles.excerpt: Dementia risk, cognitive decline, and mental illness in children — the neuroscience of wildfire smoke is catching up to what California residents already sense. Indian-Americans in the Bay Area and LA are disproportionately exposed.
articles.image_caption: Wildfire smoke over a city skyline — fine particulate matter from these events can cross the blood-brain barrier and trigger neuroinflammation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Trial of 410 Cancer Survivors Found That Four Weeks of Gentle Yoga Reduced Insomnia, Fatigue, and Anxiety. No Medication Required.
articles.excerpt: The YOCAS programme, presented at ASCO 2026, is built on hatha and restorative yoga — practices that Indian families have known for generations. Western oncology is finally catching up.
articles.image_caption: A gentle yoga session — the kind of hatha and restorative practice now shown to significantly reduce insomnia and fatigue in cancer survivors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Study of 39,000 Women Found That Two Hours of Brisk Walking Per Week Cuts Stroke Risk by 30 Per Cent. Running Did Not Do Better.
articles.excerpt: The Women's Health Study tracked participants for twelve years. Brisk walking outperformed vigorous exercise for stroke prevention. South Asian women in the US have among the lowest physical activity rates of any demographic group.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Study Found That Coffee Reshapes Your Gut Bacteria and Improves Your Mood. Caffeine Had Nothing to Do With It.
articles.excerpt: A Nature Communications trial separated 62 adults into coffee drinkers and non-drinkers, then removed coffee for two weeks. When it came back — caffeinated or decaf — stress and depression scores dropped in both groups. The gut-brain axis, not the caffeine, was doing the work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Review of Every Major Vaping Study Since 2017 Found DNA Damage, Heavy Metals, and Early Cancer Signals. 'Safer Than Cigarettes' Was Never the Same as 'Safe.'
articles.excerpt: E-cigarette aerosols contain formaldehyde, nickel, and chromium. Asian-American teens are among the fastest-growing users. Indian-American parents may be the last to notice.
articles.image_caption: E-cigarette aerosols contain DNA-damaging compounds including formaldehyde and heavy metals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Yale Study of 540,000 People Found That Your Body Can Tell the Difference Between Working Hard and Working Out. Only One of Them Protects Your Health.
articles.excerpt: New research in Nature Genetics shows leisure-time exercise activates biological pathways that workplace movement and household chores simply cannot replicate. Indian-American professionals are among the most affected.
articles.image_caption: Leisure-time exercise — the kind you choose to do — activates biological pathways that workplace movement cannot replicate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
